trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
The line must go right: up is number 10, which comes later; left is number 4, which comes later; down is number 3, which comes later.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going around the edge to (2,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going down would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
The line must go up: down is number 8, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (5,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 6. So the line goes around the edge to (1,5).
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left would force the line onto number 10 before its turn; going around the edge to (5,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,2). So the line goes up.
The line must go left: around the edge to (4,1) is number 8, which comes later.
Going down would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes left.
The line must go left: down is number 9, which comes later.
Going down would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (5,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (1,4).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.

Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.

Generation 0: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.

Jackpot! A future covers the whole board. Cashing in!
